editions.headline: VGK SWEEP AVALANCHE, PUNCH TICKET TO STANLEY CUP FINAL FOR THIRD TIME IN NINE SEASONS
editions.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights completed a stunning sweep of the Presidents' Trophy-winning Colorado Avalanche, winning Game 4 2-1 at T-Mobile Arena to advance to the Stanley Cup Final for the third time in franchise history. Mark Stone scored his second goal in as many games since returning from injury, and Carter Hart was superb with 20 saves on 21 shots. Vegas now awaits the winner of the Eastern Conference Final between Carolina (leading 2-1) and Montreal, with Game 4 scheduled for Wednesday.

games.context: Western Conference Final · Game 4 · T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas
games.series_note: VGK sweeps series 4-0 — advance to Stanley Cup Final
games.detail: Mark Stone opened the scoring 4:42 into the first period, gliding a Brayden McNabb flip pass down to himself and using a backhand-to-forehand move to beat Mackenzie Blackwood — his second goal in as many games since returning from injury. Cole Smith sealed it at 14:15 of the third, deflecting Dylan Coghlan's point shot through Blackwood's five-hole. Gabriel Landeskog made it 2-1 on a 6-on-5 deflection with 2:03 remaining, but Carter Hart held firm (20 saves). Valeri Nichushkin sat out with a lower-body injury and Nathan MacKinnon — who gutted through his knee injury — was effectively neutralized by Vegas's shutdown corps.

vgk.record_detail: 12-4 in the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs (4-0 in Western Conference Final — sweep)
vgk.series: Vegas Golden Knights swept the Colorado Avalanche 4-0 in the Western Conference Final, advancing to the Stanley Cup Final for the third time in franchise history (2018, 2023, 2026). They await the winner of Carolina vs. Montreal.
vgk.spotlight: Mark Stone scored his second goal in back-to-back games since returning from his lower-body injury, and Carter Hart posted a stellar 20/21 (.952 SV%) performance to seal the sweep. Vegas has now won 11 of their last 12 playoff games and look every bit like a team built to win the Cup. Cole Smith's redirect goal proved to be the series clincher — classic Tortorella energy hockey from the fourth line delivering when it mattered most.
notes: VGK sweep the Presidents' Trophy-winning Avalanche — only the fourth Presidents' Trophy winner swept in the conference finals in NHL history.
Mark Stone has scored in back-to-back games (G3 and G4) since returning from injury. He now has 10 points (5g, 5a) in 10 playoff GP, matching his pts-per-game pace from VGK's 2023 Cup run.
Carter Hart is now 12-3 (.929 SV%, 2.07 GAA) in the 2026 playoffs — one win shy of matching Marc-Andre Fleury's franchise record of 13 wins in a single postseason.
VGK are still without their 2026 2nd-round draft pick following the upheld appeal of the media access violation. Bruce Cassidy interview block remains in effect — Coaches' Association is monitoring.
Valeri Nichushkin (COL) sat out Game 4 with a lower-body injury, further illustrating Colorado's health disadvantage heading into the final games of their season.
vgk.next_detail: VGK await the winner of the ECF (Carolina leads Montreal 2-1). ECF Game 4 is Wednesday, May 27. Once the East is settled, the SCF schedule will be announced. If Carolina wins, Game 1 would be in Raleigh. If Montreal wins, Game 1 would be in Montreal.

tweets.text: Colorado GM Chris MacFarland is a logical target for Nashville in their GM search. Doesn't mean he's definitely going — or that Nashville is the only team interested — but if I'm looking for names, his is near the top.

On the VGK-Cassidy situation: nothing has changed. Vegas is still blocking all interview requests. The Coaches' Association has made its displeasure clear, but the league says Vegas is within its contractual rights.

Preliminary discussions between NJ GM Sunny Mehta and Nico Hischier's agent have been described as 'amicable and positive.' But teams like LA, Minnesota, and Montreal are watching closely if he hits the trade market.
On Malkin: I had been told this was coming. One year at $5.5M with significant bonus escalators. The Big Three stays together in Pittsburgh — for now.
Contacted Mike Babcock about the Oilers coaching rumors. His reply: 'Dregs, I'm retired. Loving it.' That's a hard no from Babcock on Edmonton.
On Leafs coaching and David Carle: real interest exists. But Carle is evaluating Toronto as much as Toronto is evaluating him. The family consideration for someone rooted in Denver is also real.

Manny Malhotra is the frontrunner for the Vancouver Canucks head coaching job. If that happens — and it seems increasingly likely — it complicates Toronto's search significantly, as Malhotra was also on their radar.
Tampa Bay Lightning assistant Jeff Halpern is a name to watch for the Leafs. Real organizational respect around the league for his work with Tampa's forward group.

Auston Matthews needs to see how John Chayka approaches this summer before he commits to staying in Toronto. Per sources, he's not pushing for a trade — but he's not ruling anything out. He has a full NMC and knows his leverage.
The Leafs' message to other teams this summer: Matthews is the one untouchable player on their roster. That tracks — but it also means everyone else is potentially available.

Toronto is in the early steps of their coaching search. Interviews expected to begin next week. They'll reach out to multiple clubs for permission to speak with candidates currently under contract elsewhere.
Hearing the Canucks are moving quickly on the coaching search. Malhotra is the frontrunner but the team hasn't officially offered anything yet. Expect a decision within 10 days.

League sources tell me there's preliminary discussion between Ottawa and Buffalo around a potential player swap this summer. Neither side has committed to anything, but there's mutual interest in solving cap and roster needs.

editions.headline: VGK ERASE 3-GOAL DEFICIT, AVALANCHE ON BRINK OF SWEEP
editions.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights mounted a stunning comeback from a 3-0 first-period deficit to defeat the Colorado Avalanche 5-3 in Game 3 of the Western Conference Final, taking a commanding 3-0 series lead. Mark Stone returned from a lower-body injury and scored a power-play goal in his first game since Round 2 against Anaheim. Nathan MacKinnon absorbed a puck to the right knee in the second period and was limited the rest of the way, clouding Colorado's outlook ahead of Game 4 on Tuesday. VGK can complete the sweep and punch their ticket to the Stanley Cup Final at Ball Arena.

games.context: Western Conference Final · Game 3 · T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas
games.detail: Colorado jumped to a stunning 3-0 lead on goals from Gabriel Landeskog, Nazem Kadri, and Jack Drury before the Knights struck back with five unanswered. Mark Stone (PP), William Karlsson, and Tomas Hertl erased the deficit; Keegan Kolesar and Brett Howden (EN) sealed it. Mitch Marner and Kaedan Korczak each picked up two assists. Carter Hart was brilliant with 32 saves on 35 shots. MacKinnon blocked a Shea Theodore slapshot off his right knee in the second period and was limited the rest of the game.

news.headline: NHL Denies VGK Appeal; Golden Knights Lose 2026 2nd-Round Pick, Tortorella Fined $100K
news.detail: Vegas's appeal of their media access violation penalty was denied by the NHL. The Golden Knights forfeited their 2026 second-round draft pick and coach John Tortorella was fined $100,000 after blocking locker-room access following the series-clinching win over Anaheim. GM Kelly McCrimmon and President George McPhee attended a hearing in New York; the sanctions were upheld in full.

news.headline: VGK Blocking Bruce Cassidy Interviews; NHL Coaches’ Association Monitoring
news.detail: The Vegas Golden Knights have denied both the Edmonton Oilers and LA Kings permission to interview fired head coach Bruce Cassidy. Cassidy was let go in late March but remains under contract. The NHL Coaches’ Association said Tuesday it is closely monitoring the situation. Both Friedman and LeBrun confirmed teams have been rebuffed.

news.headline: Mark Stone Returns, Scores in Comeback Win — A Timely Boost for VGK’s Cup Hopes

The Stone-Marner connection immediately reinvigorated the VGK top line and creates matchup headaches for any future opponent.

Montreal has struggled at home in the 2026 playoffs, losing 4 of 6 home games. Andersen is the best goalie remaining in the playoffs per save percentage.

editions.headline: Canadiens Shock the 'Canes With Four-Goal First
editions.summary: The Montreal Canadiens detonated on Carolina in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Final, scoring four times in the opening period en route to a stunning 6-2 road victory at Lenovo Center. Juraj Slafkovsky (2G, 1A), Nick Suzuki (3A), Cole Caufield (1G, 1A), and Jakob Dobes (24 saves) starred as Montreal handed the previously unbeaten Hurricanes their first loss of the 2026 playoffs. Meanwhile the Western Conference Final resumes tonight in Denver, with Vegas looking to go up 2-0 on Colorado after Game 1's 4-2 road win.

games.context: Eastern Conference Final · Game 1 · Lenovo Center, Raleigh, NC
games.detail: Montreal pounced for four first-period goals on a Carolina team that had been idle for 11+ days. Cole Caufield and Phillip Danault scored in the opening four minutes, Alexandre Texier added a third, and Ivan Demidov finished a breakaway to shock the Hurricanes 4-1 by the midway point of the first. Juraj Slafkovsky added two third-period goals — his second an empty-netter — to complete the route. Nick Suzuki totaled three assists. Jakob Dobes stopped 24 shots for Montreal. For Carolina — 11-0 entering this series — it was a jarring first loss of the 2026 postseason.

tweets.text: NHL denied the Golden Knights' appeal. The $100K Tortorella fine and the 2026 second-round pick forfeiture both stand. No further recourse.
2026-27 salary cap officially set at $104 million. Teams were informed today. Expect aggressive movement — lots of cap space across the league.
Bobrovsky-to-VGK chatter is real but complicated by salary retention. If Florida eats some, the Knights would listen. Could make sense for both sides.
Blackhawks are willing to trade Ilya Mikheyev's UFA signing rights. He rejected an extension. Chicago looking to bundle him in a larger deal.
VGK-Andersson extension: as expected, agreement in principle. Official July 1 once Pietrangelo clears to offseason LTIR. Multi-year deal.
Panthers have opened quiet conversations on Reinhart. He's one year from UFA. Suitors are out there but Panthers aren't in a rush to move him cheap.
Minnesota's Quinn Hughes extension is the No. 1 priority for Bill Guerin before any trade pursuit. Hughes wants to stay — both sides optimistic.
Wild made a real offer to St. Louis for Robert Thomas. Blues rejected it. Thomas has a NTC but Guerin isn't giving up on finding a top-line center.
Columbus-Garland talks: CBJ came close at the deadline. The ask from Vancouver remains a first-round pick plus. Expect this to resurface this summer.
Alex Tuch camp is seeking Kempe-level money ($10.6M AAV). Buffalo countering in the $8.5-9.5M range. Gap is real but both sides want to get it done.
Panthers offseason will be more eventful than people expect. Bobrovsky situation, Reinhart extension talks, and a need for faster defensemen all in play.
Reached out to Mike Babcock on Edmonton rumors. His response: 'Dregs, I'm retired. Loving it.' Oilers coaching search is ongoing — no frontrunner yet.
Blues-Sabres Robert Thomas talks: Buffalo is the frontrunner. St. Louis asking price involves a first, a top prospect, and a roster piece. Sabres working it.
Golden Knights and Hurricanes are the two teams most engaged on Bobrovsky. If FLA eats enough salary, CAR could make sense financially.
Jordan Kyrou's name has come up in multiple conversations this week. Blues asking for a top defensive prospect, a first, and term in a sign-and-trade.
Tristan Jarry situation in Edmonton becomes a problem if they don't upgrade in net. Two years left at $5.4M. Would need to attach a pick to move him.
Toronto GM John Chayka open to listening on any Maple Leaf except Auston Matthews. Nylander and Rielly both have NMCs — that constrains options significantly.
Matthews-Chayka meeting expected within the next two weeks. Matthews has 2 years remaining. Outcome of those talks shapes everything else Toronto does.
Chayka framing the summer as a retool, not a rebuild. He believes the core is salvageable — just needs pieces around it and cap flexibility.
Toronto won the draft lottery — selecting first overall. Gavin McKenna is the expected pick. That pick becomes a negotiating chip regardless.
The VGK sanction story framed their WCF entry negatively. Instead of celebrating the best scoring race in conference final history, it's been fines and forfeitures.
Hellebuyck situation in Winnipeg: final year of his deal at $6.17M. If Jets fall short of their Cup window, would moving him actually make sense?
Lafrenière on the market: Rangers willing to discuss him in a package. He's young and has term but hasn't taken the step NYR hoped for.
Mikheyev (CHI) signing rights: Blackhawks looking to bundle him in a larger deal as a sweetener. Not expecting a big return on the rights alone.
Owen Tippett injury impact: Flyers' offseason direction could shift depending on his recovery timeline. Teams that had him targeted are pausing.
Thin UFA market + $104M cap = trade-heavy offseason. Teams that need centers, goalies, and RHDs will be forced to pay a premium in trades.
Tuch staying in Buffalo: would be a little surprised if he leaves. Deal is close enough. Expect it finalized around draft time.
Kyrou, Lafrenière, Hellebuyck, Tippett (health permitting) — the trade market this summer could be more star-studded than any in recent memory.
Buffalo-Thomas fits. Sabres have the assets and a clear center need. Blues would be selling to a conference rival but the price makes that easier to stomach.
Montreal's success changes their off-season dynamic completely. They were sellers a year ago — they're buyers now. Slafkovsky, Demidov, Caufield as untouchables.
Patrik Laine is UFA this summer. Canadiens will not re-sign him. His agent says he wants a two-year prove-it deal to rebuild value. Interesting market.
Carolina falls flat in Game 1 after 11 days off. 6-2. Storyline of the conference final suddenly flipped — Montreal is the team to beat.
Toronto situation brewing all summer. Chayka has to make a call on Matthews before the trade market opens fully. Everything else flows from that.
Wild paid a massive price for Quinn Hughes. A first-line center acquisition is next. Hard to imagine they stop there — Guerin is all-in on this window.
Oilers coaching search going wider than expected. At least five candidates. No frontrunner. Could be a longer process than the organization would like.
Vancouver not ready to move Garland. The ask is a first plus a real return — Columbus won't go there yet. This one drags into the summer.
Thatcher Demko extension is Vancouver's summer priority. If that gets done, Canucks become sellers of depth. If not — his name enters trade talks.
J.T. Miller's time in Vancouver is over. Canucks moving away from big, older contracts. Finding a taker at his cap hit ($8M) is the challenge.
Elias Pettersson extension talks ongoing — both sides want it done before July 1. No concern this gets messy but term and AAV still being negotiated.
If Connor Hellebuyck hits the open market it changes everything. Every Cup contender picks up the phone. Jets are aware of what they have.
Florida possibly trading Bobrovsky signals a full reset. If they move Reinhart too — this Panthers era is over. Significant rebuild territory.
Winnipeg offer sheet on Dorofeyev is plausible but VGK has the cap space to match and will. Still forces VGK's hand on his next deal earlier than planned.
Montreal's young core is completely untouchable after that Game 1 performance. Slafkovsky, Demidov, Caufield, Dobes — the Habs are building something real.
Carolina after Game 1: the 11-day layoff was real. They looked flat and slow. Still elite — but they've been exposed as vulnerable. Game 2 is must-watch.
Rangers face real decisions on Lafrenière and Chytil. Drury wants better up the middle. One of those two becomes the centerpiece of an acquisition.
Islanders are quietly active. More cap room than people realize. They've been making calls on top-6 forwards. Don't sleep on them as a summer destination.
New Jersey committed to keeping Hischier and Jack Hughes — those are off the table. But depth pieces could move to create cap flexibility this summer.
NYR-Islanders rivalry gets a subplot: both teams will be in the market this summer. Expect them to bid on similar targets. Drury vs. Matheson: round one.
Devils sat 11 players who were above replacement level this year — they have real trade chips. The question is whether any of that becomes a star.

editions.headline: CANES WIN OT THRILLER, LEAD ECF 2-1; VGK SWEEP ATTEMPT TONIGHT
editions.summary: Andrei Svechnikov scored at 14:06 of overtime to lift the Carolina Hurricanes past the Montreal Canadiens 3-2 in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Final, giving Carolina a 2-1 series lead. The Hurricanes are now a perfect 5-0 in overtime this postseason, and Frederik Andersen was dominant facing just 13 shots as Montreal outshot Carolina 35-38. In the west, the Vegas Golden Knights gear up for a sweep opportunity tonight in Game 4 at T-Mobile Arena — VGK leads COL 3-0 — with Nathan MacKinnon's status uncertain after a knee injury and Cale Makar expected to play. VGK's appeal of their 2nd-round draft pick forfeiture (for media violations under Tortorella) was denied.

games.context: Eastern Conference Final · Game 3 · Bell Centre, Montreal
games.detail: The Hurricanes dominated possession — outshooting Montreal 38-13 in regulation — but needed overtime when Lane Hutson's third-period goal tied it 2-2. Shayne Gostisbehere and Taylor Hall scored in regulation for Carolina; Mike Matheson opened the scoring for the Habs. Svechnikov took a Seth Jarvis feed above the right circle and scored through a Sebastian Aho screen at 14:06 of OT to silence the Bell Centre crowd. Andersen needed just 11 saves; Dobes faced 38 and stopped 35. CAR is now 5-0 in overtime this postseason. Game 4 is Wednesday at Bell Centre (8 p.m. ET, TNT).
